CAMS 501: This course establishes the historical, linguistic and cultural foundations of proto-Indo-European, the reconstructed ancestral language which underlies most of the languages of Europe and some of the languages of western Asia and the Indian subcontinent.
CAMS 520: Advanced study of Sumerian grammar and cuneiform writing through the reading of Sumerian literary texts.
CAMS 521: Advanced study of Akkadian grammar and the cuneiform script through the reading of texts in various dialects.
CAMS 522: Overview of the Semitic language family and introduction to its comparative linguistic study.
CAMS 530: This course offers rotating topics in the study of ancient Judaism.
CAMS 535: This course offers rotating topics in the advanced study of the history and cultures of the Ancient Near East, including Mesopotamia, Egypt, and the Levant.
CAMS 540: This course is a graduate seminar that explores topics in the disciplinary and interdisciplinary areas of ancient Roman studies.
CAMS 550: This proseminar aims to provide students a foundation for scholarly work in any of the disciplines included within Ancient Mediterranean Studies.
CAMS 560: The specific aim of this seminar is to provide a research experience in one of the disciplines included within Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies.
CAMS 594: Supervised student activities on research projects identified on an individual or small-group basis.
CAMS 596: Creative projects, including nonthesis research, that are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
CAMS 597: Formal courses given on a topical or special interest subject which may be offered infrequently.
